Messages.Author: Martin Engelhardt
Messages.Body:
Gary S Cerefice (cere...@athena.mit.edu) wrote:
: Hello all,

: Anyone have the spoilers on the new cards released in V:TES?

Hi Gary,

I saw one of the new cards at the Spiel 95 in Essen on Thursday.
It is an out of turn Master, costs 3 Pool and has the following
effect:
If you are bled for three or more (or more than three, don't
remember), you may play Archon Investigation (cards name, of
course). This will burn the bleeding Vampire.

BTW, the new cards look great. Every type of card now has a different
Background, they still have black borders, but now there is a thin
ca. 1 mm red line between the border an the background. Oh, and the
background of the reaction cards is IMO the best looking. It is not
white, as some might have feared, it looks like a shattered window.

Before anyone askes: the cards were from a test run, they are not
available yet. The WoTC rep sait that the unlimited version would hit
the stores in mid-november, with the DS expansion following three
weeks later. Let's wait and see (and hope).

Happy bleeding,

Martin

Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
Martin Jamieson <mm32...@minmet.uq.oz.au> wrote:
>Either way its an out of turn master so anyone could use it (including
>the people not being bled), a 3 pool burn by two methusalahs isn't too
>much to pay to get rid of a nasty justicar or something. Then there's the
>problem of the new 11 blood inner circle members they are bringing in
>with dark soveriegns, a base bleed of 3...... why bother if you can't
>bleed with them anyway...

First, Archon Investigation can only be played if you are the one being
bleed. Second, the minion has to be attempting a bleed in excess of 3
to use AI, not of 3, so the Inner Circle members can bleed normally
without fear of it. Third, AI doesn't make the Inner Circle members'
bleeds obselete any more than it makes superior Conditioning obsolete.
If you're totally paranoid about AI, then you never bleed for more than 3,
but if you take a chance occasionally, or catch someone when they've already
burned their next master phase action, then you should be fine.

Tom Wylie rec.games.trading-cards.* Network Representative for
aa...@cats.ucsc.edu Wizards of the Coast, Inc.

a pulse of the canaille - a sure sign of a death wish . Your argument about

going to be without their next master phase ? Hint guys , cut it back to

Saying that the IC members with Dominate can never use bleed modifiers safely
because of Archon Investigation is like saying a vampire without Fortitude can
never engage a Gangrel in combat safely because of Protean. Yes, you will
get hosed sometimes, but you'll be fine at other times. You have to look
at the situation and decide what the risk is. People are not going to be
loading up their decks with Archon Investigation, because it only helps
in a relatively limited situation, so big bleeders will be ok much of the time.

I'll agree with "gang up" being a sign of degeneracy, but as Johan said,
"In a lot of gaming groups". In the places I've been, S&B "gang up" has
only been the case under 4-card limits. There are many other instances
that "gang up" is legitimately(sp?) needed. If there is only one
political deck at a table, it has a free hand. The TABLE better stop it
before it gets out of control. If there is a monster combat deck eating
up its prey, and it has a weak grandprey, the TABLE better stop it.

Why?

With the vote deck, having a free hand to do whatever it wants whenever a
vote gets to the table is handing the Methuselah a ton of power.
Similarly with combat monster destroying its preu with the weak
grandprey. Its virtually guaranteed 2 VP and 12 pool unless the table
does something to stop it. The same with a S&B in the same position as
the combat deck.

Messages.Author: Mr JA Chapman
Messages.Body:
T.J. Hull (t...@nwlink.com) wrote:
: Has anyone thought of the fact that playing a bleed deck that never

: chooses to bleed more than three can cause/aggravate a hand jam in a
: prey that hold Archon Investigation?

:
: TJH
Problem is even 1 AI can wreck an opponents day if hes using mid
sized to large vamps....Its not the sort of card you need a lot of and if you
end up with a predator whos only doing <=3 bleeds you can just toss any
multiples that come out . After someones had a big vamp burnt a few times
theyll just stop trying (unless theyre playing malks because of perceived
similarities in personality) .
How stupid would it be if there was another OOTM that prevented
damage and burnt a vampire if it did more than 2 damage in a single strike
in combat . Yes you could still have a combat deck...theoretically - but
it would suck pretty badly . The closest thing we had to this was Rotschreck
an aggro - but this was just so popular in its 'spoiler' interpretation
that it was ignored in favour of house rules . And surprise,surprise what card
disappeared in VTES?...........
The card is an attempt to hose rampant bleed decks . The problem is
that malks S&B was the main tactic that needed to be limited , but this is
probably the least affected . Using the madness network to bleed the person
in their own turn (unless the card has changed significantly - I havent
been able to view the new ones) Malks can still bleed for heaps without
worrying about AI .
ALso it furthers the trend towards using lots of small vamps . Most
of the successful decks that ive seen are already based on <6 vampires .
This card will see even fewer decks with large vampires , both cutting down
the penatly if one gets burnt and allowing multiple small bleeds rathe than
just one big one . This once again cuts
back on the number of possible strategies and decreasing the variety .
It does wreck decks like torreador and tremere bash and bleed and tap
and bleed decks which typically rely on one large bleed a round . It was not
needed especially with the other , somewhat fairer bleed killers . The new
intercept card (whatever its name is ) is a much better response to S&B
and specifically targets this tactic (ie it was the sort of card required) .
JUsticar retribution can also be used to get rid of bleed monsters , but can
both be defeated by a vote or intercepted . Cross table votes which cant be
intercepted (by the victim) were the big danger here,but most of the targetted
vamps (ie PUlse of The Canaille or IC members) have auspex and as such
can use Eagles sight to stop this happening in most cases .
What we have here is a spoiler whose effects are in no way reflected by
its cost . Unbalanced cards like this IMO are the most detrimental to game
balance (though some only become unbalanced in combos like zipgun -DBR) .
For a small cost we have a method to dissuade people from big bleeds or to
throw an unjust and painful penalty at the bleeder . Jyhad used to (in most
cases) require more than a 'insert this one card to wreck entire strategy'
solution . This made for better , more thinking , games .

JA Chapman

In article <Pine.NXT.3.91.951119185731.518C-100000@pentode> The Corrupter <sull...@cslab.uwlax.edu> writes:

>I'll agree with "gang up" being a sign of degeneracy, but as Johan said,
>"In a lot of gaming groups". In the places I've been, S&B "gang up" has
>only been the case under 4-card limits. There are many other instances
>that "gang up" is legitimately(sp?) needed. If there is only one
>political deck at a table, it has a free hand. The TABLE better stop it
>before it gets out of control. If there is a monster combat deck eating
>up its prey, and it has a weak grandprey, the TABLE better stop it.
>
>Why?
>
>With the vote deck, having a free hand to do whatever it wants whenever a
>vote gets to the table is handing the Methuselah a ton of power.
>Similarly with combat monster destroying its preu with the weak
>grandprey. Its virtually guaranteed 2 VP and 12 pool unless the table
>does something to stop it. The same with a S&B in the same position as
>the combat deck.

That still somewhat depends on how the player view `victory'.
If they see the player with the most VP as winner and everybody else
loses, then they will gang up in the described situations.
But if they view 0 VP as a loss, 1 VP as a draw, 2VP as a marginal
victory and more than 2 VP a big win, then it might be better to
concentrate on your prey and guarantee a VP or 2 while ignoring the
other side of the table. (Even if I contribute to ganging-up and
knowck down that biggie, I may well end up with 0 VP, especially
if the biggie is my grand-prey.)

My conjecture is that the `one vote/push per meth' (with the stricter
rule that the calling Meth. cannot push above his one vote on the
P.A. card) rule will really restrict the power of vote decks.
It might even encourage every player to put a few votes in his
deck, since a random vote or two is more significant when there
are simply less votes cast. We'll also see more negotiated votes,
and some more intelligent use of cards like Bewitching Orations,
etc. (Now, you can't use BO to pass a vote in a non-voting
deck if there's another vote deck at the table.)
